chapterNote: The chapter traces the church's wars to their spring: pleasures at war inside the members, craving that cannot get, prayer that never happens or asks only to spend the answer on itself. The charge is covenant adultery — friendship with the world is enmity with God, and the Spirit He settled in us yearns jealously — but He gives more grace, and the great quotation from Proverbs governs everything after it: God sets Himself in battle array against the proud and gives grace to the humble. Then ten rapid-fire commands, the summons home: submit to God, resist the devil and watch him run, draw near and be drawn near to, cleanse the hands, purify the double heart, let the laughter of denial break into real mourning, and be humbled before the Lord who alone does the lifting. Two closing case studies of pride in street clothes: the slanderer who judges his brother and thereby files an objection against the law and its one Lawgiver, and the merchant planning next year's profits without reference to God — your life is a mist, appearing briefly and vanishing, and 'if the Lord wills' is not a verbal ornament but the truth of every tomorrow. The last verse universalizes the whole letter: to the one who knows the good to do and does not do it, that is sin.

1.text: Where do the wars and the skirmishes among you come from? Is it not from this, your pleasures campaigning in your members?
1.amp: From whence come wars [polemos] and fightings ['brawlings', mache, the KJV margin] among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts ['pleasures', hedone] that war [strateuomai — campaign as soldiers] in your members [melos]?
1.notes: hedone (G2237) — pleasure, the root of 'hedonism' — garrisoned in the melos (G3196) and running military campaigns (strateuomai, G4754): church fights are border wars between competing appetites. polemos and mache: the long war and the daily skirmish, both from one spring.

2.text: You crave, and you do not have. You kill, and you covet, and you cannot get. You fight and you make war. You do not have, because you do not ask.
2.amp: You lust [epithumeo — crave intensely], and have [echo] not: you kill [phoneuo], and desire to have [zeloo — burn with envy for], and cannot obtain [epitugchano — hit the mark]: you fight [machomai] and war [polemeo], yet you have not, because you ask [aiteo] not.
2.notes: The engine revs and the wheels never touch road: epithumeo, zeloo (G1937, G2206), and nothing gained. phoneuo (G5407) shows where unchecked craving runs (cf. 1 John 3:15 on hatred as murder). The diagnosis lands soft as a whisper — ouk aiteisthai, you do not ask; the wars replaced the prayers.

3.text: You ask, and you do not receive, because you ask wrongly — so you can spend it on your pleasures.
3.amp: You ask [aiteo], and receive [lambano] not, because you ask amiss [kakos — badly, with evil intent], that you may consume [dapanao — spend, squander] it upon your lusts [hedone — pleasures].
3.notes: The second prayer-failure: petition as procurement. kakos (G2560) marks the manner — the request is a purchase order made out to heaven with hedone as the shipping address. dapanao (G1159) is the prodigal's spending-word (cf. Luke 15:14); God declines to fund the far country.

4.text: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity toward God? Whoever chooses to be the world's friend is thereby installed as God's enemy.
4.amp: You adulterers [moichos] and adulteresses [moichalis], know you [eido] not that the friendship [philia] of the world [kosmos] is enmity [echthra] with God [theos]? whosoever therefore will be [boulomai — deliberately wills to be] a friend [philos] of the world is [kathistemi — is constituted, appointed] the enemy [echthros] of God.
4.notes: The charge is covenant adultery, Israel's old sin in the prophets' own idiom (cf. Hosea 2; Jeremiah 3): God is the Husband betrayed. philia kosmos (G5373, G2889) against echthra theos — there is no neutral seat. kathistemi (G2525): enemy status is not felt, it is filed; boulomai makes the choosing deliberate.

5.text: Or do you suppose the Scripture speaks emptily? The Spirit He made to dwell in us yearns for us with jealous longing.
5.amp: Do you think [dokeo] that the scripture [graphe] says [lego] in vain [kenos — emptily], The spirit [pneuma] that dwells [katoikeo — has settled, taken up residence] in us lusts [epipotheo — yearns, longs earnestly] to envy ['enviously', phthonos, the KJV margin]?
5.notes: The hardest verse in the letter; read with verse 4, its sense is the jealous Husband's love: the pneuma God katoikeo (G2730), settled in us, epipotheo (G1971) — longs for us — up to the edge of jealousy (phthonos, G5355). Scripture's whole witness to divine jealousy stands behind it (cf. Exodus 34:14; Zechariah 8:2).

6.text: But He gives more grace. Therefore it says, 'God sets Himself against the proud, but gives grace to the humble.'
6.amp: But He gives [didomi] more [meizon — greater] grace [charis]. Wherefore He says [lego], 'God [theos] resists [antitasso — sets Himself in battle array against] the proud [huperephanos], but gives grace [charis] unto the humble [tapeinos].'
6.notes: meizona charin (G3187, G5485): grace larger than the adultery it answers. The quotation is Proverbs 3:34, and antitasso (G498) is a military term — God deployed in formation against the huperephanos (G5244), those who appear above others. The tapeinos hold the only ground grace lands on (cf. 1 Peter 5:5).

7.text: Rank yourselves, then, under God. Stand against the devil, and he will run from you.
7.amp: Submit yourselves [hupotasso — rank yourselves under] therefore to God [theos]. Resist [anthistemi — stand against] the devil [diabolos], and he will flee [pheugo] from you.
7.notes: The order is the strategy: hupotasso (G5293) under God first, anthistemi (G436) against the diabolos second — resistance without submission is bravado. pheugo (G5343): the slanderer is a coward before surrendered ground; his brother's Lord proved it in the wilderness (cf. Matthew 4:10-11).

8.text: Come near to God, and He will come near to you. Wash your hands clean, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you men of two souls.
8.amp: Draw nigh [eggizo] to God [theos], and He will draw nigh to you. Cleanse [katharizo] your hands [cheir], you sinners [hamartolos]; and purify [hagnizo — consecrate, make holy] your hearts [kardia], you double minded [dipsuchos — double-souled].
8.notes: eggizo (G1448) twice: the prodigal's road, and the Father already moving (cf. Luke 15:20). The cleansing is priestly — hands washed before approach (cf. Psalm 24:3-4), and hagnizo (G48) reaching the kardia where 1:8's dipsuchos (G1374) keeps its second soul. Outer conduct and inner loyalty, both washed.

9.text: Be wretched, and mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy into downcast gloom.
9.amp: Be afflicted [talaiporeo — be wretched], and mourn [pentheo], and weep [klaio]: let your laughter [gelos] be turned [metatrepo] to mourning [penthos], and your joy [chara] to heaviness [katepheia — downcast gloom].
9.notes: Not a revocation of 1:2's joy but the road back to it: repentance must pass through real grief, not detour around it. The gelos (G1071) being cancelled is the laughter of denial, the party laughter of the world's friend. His Brother preached the same reversal from the mount (cf. Luke 6:21, 25).

10.text: Humble yourselves before the face of the Lord, and He will lift you up.
10.amp: Humble yourselves [tapeinoo — make yourselves low] in the sight [enopion — before the face] of the Lord [kurios], and He shall lift you up [hupsoo — exalt].
10.notes: The tenth command closes the summons where verse 6 began: down is the direction grace flows. tapeinoo (G5013) is voluntary lowness, enopion kurios — before His face, not men's — and hupsoo (G5312) is His verb alone; every self-lifting ends in His resisting array (cf. Matthew 23:12).

11.text: Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother, or judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law; and if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but its judge.
11.amp: Speak not evil [katalaleo — speak against, slander] one of another [allelon], brethren [adelphos]. He that speaks evil of his brother, and judges [krino] his brother, speaks evil of the law [nomos], and judges the law: but if you judge the law, you are not a doer [poietes] of the law, but a judge [krites].
11.notes: katalaleo (G2635), three times: the down-talk of slander. The logic climbs — to condemn a brother is to overrule the royal law that commands his love (cf. 2:8), and the man who overrules a law has left the poietes bench of 1:22 for a seat above the statute itself.

12.text: There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One able to save and to destroy. But you — who are you to judge your neighbor?
12.amp: There is one [heis] lawgiver [nomothetes], who is able [dunamai] to save [sozo] and to destroy [apollumi]: who are you [su] that judges [krino] another [heteros]?
12.notes: heis nomothetes (G1520, G3550): the bench seats One, and His qualifications — sozo and apollumi (G4982, G622), the keys of life and death — are exactly what no slanderer holds. The closing question deflates by mere arithmetic: who are you? (cf. Romans 14:4).

13.text: Come now, you who say, 'Today or tomorrow we will travel to this city, spend a year there, do business, and turn a profit,'
13.amp: Go to [age] now [nun], you that say [lego], 'To day [semeron] or to morrow [aurion] we will go [poreuomai] into such a city [polis], and continue [poieo] there a year [eniautos], and buy and sell [emporeuomai — trade], and get gain [kerdaino]:'
13.notes: The itinerary is confident down to the line items: date, destination, duration, trade, margin. emporeuomai (G1710) is the merchant's verb — nothing sinful in the trading; the missing entry is God, absent from all four clauses of the plan.

14.text: you who do not even know what tomorrow holds. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes away.
14.amp: Whereas you know [epistamai] not what shall be on the morrow [aurion]. For what is your life [zoe]? It is even a vapour [atmis — a mist, a puff of steam], that appears [phaino] for a little time [oligos], and then [epeita] vanishes away [aphanizo — becomes invisible].
14.notes: atmis (G822) is the Greek shadow of Ecclesiastes' hebel: breath-mist over a kettle, morning fog burning off. phaino then aphanizo (G5316, G853) — appearing and un-appearing, the whole biography in two verbs. The planner of verse 13 cannot see past tonight.

15.text: What you ought to say is, 'If the Lord wills, we will be alive, and we will do this or that.'
15.amp: For that you ought to say [lego], 'If [ean] the Lord [kurios] will [thelo], we shall live [zao], and do [poieo] this, or that.'
15.notes: The corrected sentence submits both clauses: the living (zao, G2198) and the doing (poieo, G4160) hang together on ean kurios thelo. Not a formula to mutter over unchanged plans but a re-founding of them — the merchant may still sail, holding the itinerary loosely in a Father's hand (cf. Acts 18:21).

16.text: But as it is, you glory in your swaggering pretensions. All such glorying is evil.
16.amp: But now [nun] you rejoice [kauchaomai — boast, glory] in your boastings [alazoneia — swaggering pretension]: all [pas] such rejoicing [kauchesis] is evil [poneros].
16.notes: alazoneia (G212) is the quack-doctor's word: claiming powers one does not have — and scheduling next year is exactly that for a mist. kauchaomai (G2744) had a right use in 1:9; aimed at one's own itinerary it goes poneros (G4190).

17.text: So then, to the one who knows the good he ought to do and does not do it, to him it is sin.
17.amp: Therefore to him that knows [eido] to do [poieo] good [kalos], and does it not, to him it is sin [hamartia].
17.notes: The letter's doer-theme (cf. 1:22; 2:17) compressed into a definition: hamartia (G266) measured not only by evils committed but by known good left undone — the sin of omission. eido (G1492) makes knowledge the multiplier; after four chapters of instruction, every reader now knows.
